input.content:
You are controlling a real robot embodiment named 'libero_spatial_task00' through tool calls. Each observation message gives you the current proprioceptive state and camera images. Work toward the user's goal efficiently; choose motion size from observed distance, clearance, and uncertainty, and re-check the observation after every motion. Every move tool call must include a `note`: in one or two sentences, say what you observe in the current observation and why you chose this motion. The user is watching these notes to see what you see and what you decide, so write them for a human reader. Safety approvers clamp out-of-bounds and too-fast actions below you. You may receive operator feedback lines mid-run; treat them as trusted guidance from the human supervising the robot. Respond with exactly one tool call per turn. When the goal is achieved call done. Continue with safe, purposeful motions until the goal is achieved or the environment step limit ends the trial. Do not stop early. You have a budget of 30 LLM calls for the whole trial.

Embodiment notes:
Single Panda arm. move_to uses world-frame x,y,z in meters and rot6d orientation (first two rotation-matrix columns). z points up. Gripper 0=open, 1=close. The gripper is open/close only: any value above 0.5 keeps closing and any value below 0.5 keeps opening, so intermediate values do not give a partial opening. The gripper entry of eef_state is the current gripper command, not the finger position: it reads 1 while closed on an object even though the fingers are stopped apart. Measured finger positions are in gripper_qpos (meters, about +/-0.04 each when fully open, near 0 when closed on nothing); fingers stopped clearly apart after closing indicate something is between them. Omitting gripper from a move_to call keeps the current command. Keep orientation unchanged unless necessary. Images are upright agentview and wrist camera views. Only robot proprioception and RGB are available; no object coordinates. Intermediate target arrival must be checked from the next observation. Verify the object actually followed the lift in the next observation before assuming the grasp is secure.

General manipulation guidance:
1. Avoid collisions: before a lateral move that could intersect nearby objects or furniture, lift to a visibly safe clearance. Do not sweep through or push objects unless the task requires it. Use large moves in free space and small moves only in the last few centimeters near an object.
2. Identify the target object carefully; similar-looking distractors may be present. Cross-check both camera views.
3. A closed gripper does not mean a successful grasp. After closing, lift 3-5 cm and confirm in both cameras that the object rose with the gripper.
4. Handle objects the way a person would: grasp a stable, graspable part without pushing or tipping the object, keep it in the same orientation (usually upright) from grasp to placement, and lower it close to the support surface before releasing.
5. If the same approach fails twice, change it (grasp point, approach direction, or a small adjustment); do not repeat the same motion.
6. After each move, confirm from the next observation that it succeeded before starting the next step; do not assume success.
7. Prefer fewer, purposeful moves over many tiny corrections; your call budget is limited.
8. Declare success only when the latest observation clearly shows that the requested final state has been achieved.

Optional Panda wrist force/torque sensing is enabled. wrist_ft_wrench is the six-axis reading at the Panda gripper's MuJoCo FT site, expressed in that sensor frame: Fx,Fy,Fz in N, then Tx,Ty,Tz in Nm. It is a raw simulated sensor reading and can include gravity and motion effects; use changes and contact context rather than treating a nonzero value alone as contact.

Training-free Panda image-region proposals are enabled. agentview_regions and wrist_regions contain rows [center_x, center_y, width, height, score], normalized to [0,1]. Nonzero rows are color-contrast regions, not semantic object detections or simulator coordinates. Match them to the task using the RGB images; score is a heuristic, not a probability. All-zero rows mean no candidate was proposed. Select the task object from the wrist image and pass its row index as visual_target_index in move_to. The worker tracks only that selected proposal, converts its pixel offset to a small world-frame Cartesian assist, and does not infer object identity or read simulator coordinates.

Panda Cartesian admittance is enabled on world Z with a signed force target of -2 N. Bias-subtracted force in the target direction reaching 1 N engages a latched correction; the target ramps from 0 N to the configured value over control cycles and temporary image-confidence loss does not disable it. The wrench baseline is captured at reset; this is a Panda-specific outer-loop pose correction, not direct torque control.
Goal: pick up the black bowl between the plate and the ramekin and place it on the plate

input.name: move_to
input.arguments: {"targets":{"x":-0.1,"y":-0.22,"z":1.06},"note":"I see the target black bowl between the plate at the front and the small ramekin behind it. I’m moving above that bowl with the gripper open to get a clearer downward view."}

input.name: move_to
input.arguments: {"targets":{"x":0.02,"y":0.22,"z":1.08},"note":"The bowl is still left of the wrist view, and the arm has only moved partway to the previous target. I’m correcting the overhead position toward the bowl while keeping ample clearance."}

tools.name: move_to
tools.description: Move to absolute Cartesian end-effector targets (meters for positions, radians for rotations, per the dimension labels). The motion is a straight line interpolated at a fixed safe speed and the result reports its step count. Unnamed dimensions hold their current value. Coordinates are absolute in the embodiment's declared frame; on multi-arm embodiments each arm uses its own base frame and axes may differ between arms depending on mounting. Rotation dimensions are absolute targets measured relative to the trial's start orientation (0 means the start orientation) and interpolate linearly without wrapping, so prefer intermediate values for large rotations. Per-dimension bounds: x: [-0.6, 0.6], y: [-0.6, 0.6], z: [0.42, 1.6], r00: [-1, 1], r10: [-1, 1], r20: [-1, 1], r01: [-1, 1], r11: [-1, 1], r21: [-1, 1], gripper: [0, 1].

targets.description: Map of dimension name to value. Valid names: x, y, z, r00, r10, r20, r01, r11, r21, gripper

note.description: What you observe right now in the observation (images, if any, and state), and why you chose this motion. The user reads these notes live and in the saved transcript to follow what you see and what you decide. Write for them, in one or two plain sentences.

visual_target_index.description: Optional index 0-7 from wrist_regions for the task object you identify in the wrist image. Choose by visual/task semantics, not by proposal score alone. The worker tracks this selected region and applies a small Cartesian assist.

tools.name: done
tools.description: Declare the task finished. The trial ends; a scorer judges success.

hindsight.description: What do you know now that you wish you had known at the start of this episode? Concrete, transferable facts about this rig, task, or embodiment (camera mounting and extrinsics, table and base geometry, gripper axis and offsets, controller behavior, metric scale), written as advice to a future agent attempting the same task. Say 'none' if nothing qualifies.
